steps.name: Anxious Civilian
steps.text: Hey, my bag! Don't push!

steps.name: Patrol Battalion Soldier
steps.text: There's plenty of time, folks. Don't panic, get in line, careful not to step on each other.

steps.name: Panicked Child
steps.text: Mama...

steps.name: Panicked Child
steps.text: I'm scared...

steps.name: Mother
steps.text: Don't be scared, just hold my hand and stay close.

steps.name: Panicked Child
steps.text: Where are we going?

steps.name: Mother
steps.text: There's a big storm coming.

steps.name: Mother
steps.text: So we're going to a safe place where we won't be blown away.
Massive shadows begin rising from outside the walls, blocking out the sun.
The Four Guardians of Yumen, retractable external mobile barriers known as the Wind Aegis, designed by Tumu Tianshi and built by the military's Department of Smelting and Fabrication.
For centuries, Yumen has served as Yan's border bulwark, and the Wind Aegis have been her shield, protecting her from the sandstorms, winter winds and Originium storms of the great desert.
The Three Winds shall not pass as long as the Four Guardians stand.

steps.name: Patrol Battalion Soldier
steps.text: Wow, it's so tall...

steps.name: Patrol Battalion Soldier
steps.text: I've never seen the Wind Aegis deploy in all my three years in Yumen.

steps.name: Millenion
steps.text: Nothing to gape at.

steps.name: Millenion
steps.text: Yumen's walls are tall, and fully equipped with Originium defenses. Mundane Catastrophes rarely require the Wind Aegis to be deployed, but it's not entirely unheard of.

steps.name: Millenion
steps.text: However, this is the first time that we've had to move half the city's population, as far as I know...

steps.name: Patrol Battalion Soldier
steps.text: So, er, wh-what is the class of this Catastrophe? So big not even the Wind Aegis could hold it back?
The Wind Aegis lock into place, steel plates interlocked so tightly not even the wind can get through.
Long lines of civilians move away from the walls in the shadows that the Wind Aegis cast. Perhaps comforted by the sturdy presence of the barriers, the crowd calms down after some initial chaos.
The poplars that grow on the borderlands have grown used to the wind and sand.

steps.name: Millenion
steps.text: What's the matter? Scared?

steps.name: Millenion
steps.text: Man your post. Don't think about anything else.

steps.name: Millenion
steps.text: Keep your eyes open. The Shanhaizhong are still in the city. Anything can happen with so many people moving about.

steps.name: Millenion
steps.text: Protect the commoners.

steps.name: Lungmen Agent
steps.text: You're still here?

steps.name: Lungmen Agent
steps.text: They've been broadcasting it all day. Yumen is about to run into a Catastrophe. Those on the east side need to move to shelters on the west side before noon.

steps.name: Innkeeper
steps.text: I know, I know. The Catastrophe cloud isn't here yet. I need to pack my things...

steps.name: Innkeeper
steps.text: Here it is.

steps.name: Innkeeper
steps.text: I could lose the tables, the chairs, even the building, but not this recipe book.

steps.name: Lungmen Agent
steps.text: Say, you could come with me to Lungmen, if you lost the inn.

steps.name: Innkeeper
steps.text: Don't say that!

steps.name: Lungmen Agent
steps.text: Sorry, yeah. That's bad luck.

steps.name: Lungmen Agent
steps.text: I just figured your culinary skills would do well in Lungmen too. I've had the chance to see you work up close these few days, after all.

steps.name: Innkeeper
steps.text: Nah, can't have that.

steps.name: Innkeeper
steps.text: Where would the people of Yumen get my special sauteed meat if I left?

steps.name: Lungmen Agent
steps.text: Are you a native of Yumen?

steps.name: Innkeeper
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Innkeeper
steps.text: I was born in the heartlands and went to Lungmen to seek my fortune. I came over when the cities linked, wanting to see what things were like in the north.

steps.name: Innkeeper
steps.text: Then I lost my wallet and started working at this inn to make ends meet. Now I've been the innkeeper for years.

steps.name: Innkeeper
steps.text: The building doesn't matter. Houses can be rebuilt.

steps.name: Lungmen Agent
steps.text: Absolutely.

steps.name: Lungmen Agent
steps.text: Well, I'll help you back up.
The winds are calm.
The dark, ominous mass of air is clearly visible, even from a distance, darkening part of the sky.
The Catastrophe does not seem to have moved, but the temperature is rising.
It is as though it is waiting for a gust of wind, before lashing out at the city walls.

steps.name: Ling
steps.text: Phew...

steps.name: Ling
steps.text: Come to watch my brother's duel, General?

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: Catastrophe preparations are already done. The Grandmaster wants to see whether that one is worth his trust before the Catastrophe strikes. I can't miss this.

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: Still, it seems absurd to determine the sword's ownership in this way.

steps.name: Ling
steps.text: You've been at my brother's side for decades. You would not trust his choice as a friend?

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: ...Friend.

steps.name: Ling
steps.text: Hm.

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: We have fought side-by-side, but we have never been brothers. Neither sword nor spear, nor gun nor cannon can harm your kind. How could you truly understand the camaraderie of man?

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: You remain outsiders to it all.

steps.name: Ling
steps.text: 'Outsiders'?

steps.name: Ling
steps.text: You could say that about me, but it seems unfair to apply it to my brother.

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: Man and beast are different. This has never changed.

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: You know how the imperial court views your kind.

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: An alliance can only endure when the two sides are equals. One should not wield power beyond one's control.

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: I'm not in a position to trust him unconditionally, for I'm not his equal.

steps.name: Ling
steps.text: I'm surprised you would be so frank.

steps.name: Ling
steps.text: But perhaps you underestimate yourself...
Zuo Xuanliao gazes wordlessly at the great desert beyond. The two shadows there are like two drops of ink on a great scroll.
Heaven and earth are silent.

steps.name: Ling
steps.text: It all feels like it happened yesterday.

steps.name: Ling
steps.text: We partook in more than just war. We hunted, drank, and sang together. Yumen is still Yumen. Why is it that you have worries enough to turn your hair white?

steps.name: Ling
steps.text: Does the sight of those two remind you of those golden days?

steps.name: Ling
steps.text: You say that man and beast are different, but look, a man has chosen to challenge this great barrier. Does your heart not race at a clash like that?

steps.name: Ling
steps.text: Loosen that brow of yours.

steps.name: Ling
steps.text: Care for a drink? We could even make a wager.

steps.name: Huai Tianpei
steps.text: Good, good.

steps.name: Huai Tianpei
steps.text: You finally agreed to fight me.

steps.name: Chongyue
steps.text: Sorry for making you wait.

steps.name: Huai Tianpei
steps.text: It's only been three years. I could wait longer, if you have unfinished business.
Three years ago...

steps.name: Huai Tianpei
steps.text: Hold it.

steps.name: Chongyue
steps.text: That was just one exchange.

steps.name: Huai Tianpei
steps.text: It was enough.

steps.name: Huai Tianpei
steps.text: We traded three blows in that exchange. Someone could have been hurt, if we were using our full strength.

steps.name: Huai Tianpei
steps.text: But you're holding back, and I can't use my full strength either.

steps.name: Huai Tianpei
steps.text: That's no fun.

steps.name: Chongyue
steps.text: Sparring is about restraint...

steps.name: Huai Tianpei
steps.text: Screw sparring, screw restraint! Let's have a proper fight!

steps.name: Huai Tianpei
steps.text: All the kung fu under Heaven evolved in the struggle of life and death. You're not talking like the top-ranked fighter on the Yumen Arena Board of Fame.

steps.name: Chongyue
steps.text: You have a point. However...

steps.name: Huai Tianpei
steps.text: Fine, I know, you have a job to do. You're not in a position to go all-out.

steps.name: Huai Tianpei
steps.text: When are you quitting? We'll put this off until then.

steps.name: Chongyue
steps.text: Well, I have no idea when that might be.

steps.name: Huai Tianpei
steps.text: Guesstimate it for me.

steps.name: Chongyue
steps.text: Could be three years, five, ten, maybe more.

steps.name: Huai Tianpei
steps.text: Alright. I'll wait.

steps.name: Huai Tianpei
steps.text: You're right here, after all. I'm not worried you'll run away.

steps.name: Chongyue
steps.text: There's always more to do. This is the right time and place for the fight that I owe you.

steps.name: Chongyue
steps.text: I should explain that I have my own reasons for doing this.

steps.name: Huai Tianpei
steps.text: Oh?

steps.name: Chongyue
steps.text: There's a tradition of military commanders sparring before their troops prior to a campaign, in order to inspire the men.

steps.name: Chongyue
steps.text: Yumen is about to fight a Catastrophe. This bout between you and I will inspire the warriors of the city.

steps.name: Huai Tianpei
steps.text: Suits me just fine, as long as you're not worried about losing face when I make you eat dirt in front of the whole city.

steps.name: Chongyue
steps.text: Haha...

steps.name: Chongyue
steps.text: It's been many years since someone challenged me like this.

steps.name: Huai Tianpei
steps.text: It's been many years since I've seen someone worth challenging like you.

steps.name: Huai Tianpei
steps.text: Ready to give me your all?

steps.name: Chongyue
steps.text: Hold nothing back.

steps.name: Huai Tianpei
steps.text: Victory and defeat lie in the hands of man.

steps.name: Chongyue
steps.text: Life and death lie in the hands of Heaven.

steps.name: Du Yaoye
steps.text: Did they start yet?!

steps.name: Waai Fu
steps.text: Hey, take it easy, you're injured.

steps.name: Du Yaoye
steps.text: I'm a trained kung fu fighter. I'm not so fragile.

steps.name: Du Yaoye
steps.text: There's plenty of time to rest later. Miss this fight, and I may never see one like it ever again!

steps.name: Waai Fu
steps.text: It's not that big a deal...

steps.name: Du Yaoye
steps.text: The Feline is your dad, right? The good-for-nothing old man you were talking about?

steps.name: Du Yaoye
steps.text: I definitely see the resemblance. Like father, like daughter.

steps.name: Waai Fu
steps.text: In what way?

steps.name: Du Yaoye
steps.text: The way you look before a fight.

steps.name: Du Yaoye
steps.text: Like you're gonna eat someone.

steps.name: Waai Fu
steps.text: Hmph...

steps.name: Du Yaoye
steps.text: I hear the Grandmaster's skills are almost supernatural. He hasn't fought in public in years. Some even say that he invented half the kung fu under Heaven.

steps.name: Du Yaoye
steps.text: And I hear your dad defeated that evil woman last night.

steps.name: Du Yaoye
steps.text: Who do you think will win here?

steps.name: Du Yaoye
steps.text: Silly question. Of course you want your dad to win.

steps.name: Waai Fu
steps.text: That's his business, not mine.

steps.name: Waai Fu
steps.text: I just want to see for myself how big the gap between us is.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Mr. Liang...

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: I didn't think you would be interested in such violent business.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: I ought to be here. As a friend.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: I wonder if he achieved his goal of making a name for himself.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Look at the number of eyes on this fight. It'll be the stuff of legend, no matter who wins.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: A lunatic must answer to himself before telling others who he is.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: We must all answer to ourselves.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: You...

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: I was looking for Waai Tinp—Err, Huai Tianpei before trouble found me.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: I went back to my old detective tricks and found out a few things. I have a good idea of what you're planning.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: There's probably a reason why trouble finds you.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: A big brother must look after his siblings.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: What did you hear?

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Few know that the Grandmaster is Ling's eldest brother. Seems like it's being kept a secret.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: True...

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Retrieving the Grandmaster's sword is, of course, an urgent matter, but the bigger headache is what to do with it afterwards.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: You don't want it at Yumen. Perhaps you speak for the Sui Regulator, perhaps it's your judgment as advisor to Yumen, but the Lord Exorcist won't let it go.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: You needed someone who could take the sword, someone both sides can live with.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: You just happen to have an oath-brother who is a kung fu master, and he just happens to be in Yumen.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: It didn't take much effort to guide the girl to the clinic where Huai Tianpei worked, in order to ensure his involvement.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: From Shangshu to Yumen, you always get your old friends to solve your problems. Isn't that a little lazy?

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: I don't have many friends.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Question for you.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: When did you start thinking about getting Huai Tianpei involved?

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Never mind, no need to tell me.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: *sigh*...

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: No matter how many strings you pulled behind the scenes, it was always his lifelong wish to fight the best and become the best. He might even thank you for setting the stage, if he knew.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: We are all doing what we wanted to, even if things often don't turn out the way we want.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: After all these years, perhaps he's the one who's closest to his oldest dreams.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: 'Achieve one thing in life.' Easy for him to say...

steps.name: Record Keeper
steps.text: Mr. Huai came, despite his injuries...

steps.name: Qiubai
steps.text: He would have come as long as there was a single breath left in him. He doesn't care if it's the last thing he does.

steps.name: Record Keeper
steps.text: I know Mr. Huai came to Yumen to challenge the Grandmaster, and the Grandmaster accepted the challenge. The Grandmaster has spoken of it from time to time, and I can tell you that he's no less looking forward to this than Mr. Huai is.

steps.name: Qiubai
steps.text: All kung fu fighters thirst for a good opponent.

steps.name: Qiubai
steps.text: It's an obsession, a strange one. It's natural that you don't understand.

steps.name: Record Keeper
steps.text: It's the same reason that you follow the Grandmaster.

steps.name: Qiubai
steps.text: You can actually be kind of astute at times, you know that?

steps.name: Record Keeper
steps.text: I'll head down now.

steps.name: Qiubai
steps.text: It's two masters at work. Nothing in your records will come close to what you are about to see.

steps.name: Record Keeper
steps.text: I'll try to be detailed.

steps.name: Qiubai
steps.text: Just keep your distance. You don't want to get hurt.

steps.name: Record Keeper
steps.text: Of course.
Earlier that day...

steps.name: Qiubai
steps.text: Today's the day, isn't it?

steps.name: Chongyue
steps.text: Are you ready?

steps.name: Qiubai
steps.text: The veterans say Yumen has been through many crises in the past, but nothing on this scale.

steps.name: Qiubai
steps.text: Not even you know what's going to come of it, do you?

steps.name: Chongyue
steps.text: Things are more complicated than meets the eye.
From Jiangqi to Yumen, how many times has she seen danger, seen her life hang by a thread?
Yet she did not die in the wilderness, nor did she become like the Shanhaizhong.
What is it that has kept her going?

steps.name: Qiubai
steps.text: This city has treated me well. I should do something for it.

steps.name: Qiubai
steps.text: Before that, however, I must answer to myself.

steps.name: Qiubai
steps.text: You said that you would fight me whenever I felt up to it.

steps.name: Chongyue
steps.text: I did.

steps.name: Chongyue
steps.text: Strike me, if you're ready.
Qiubai takes a step back, focuses, and raises her sword.
She knows that he knows her every move like the back of his hand.
An eye for an eye.
Is there wisdom in the saying, or is it simply a result?
How many people have fed the fins by the river fort? Should their families seek revenge on her father?
How many people would seek revenge on her, if she killed this one in front of her for the sake of her own revenge?
The cycle of vengeance never ends.
Should it really be hate that keeps her going?
How long has she been thinking about that question? The five years that she has been around this man, seeing all that he saw?
No, longer than that.
Her sword has seen blood every step of the way from Jiangqi to Yumen. How would she judge those dead by it?
That is why she came to Yumen, for revenge, and to learn.
Exact what must be exacted, and discern what must be discerned.
The sword is pulled back abruptly.
It leaves her hand and falls into a nearby ditch, sending a pack of fowlbeasts scattering in all directions.
The violence of the move almost injures her, showing none of her usual grace in practice or battle.
Her expression, however, is one of satisfaction.

steps.name: Qiubai
steps.text: That will do.

steps.name: Qiubai
steps.text: The sword has been thrust. It couldn't have killed you.

steps.name: Chongyue
steps.text: ...Correct.

steps.name: Qiubai
steps.text: I didn't let go of vengeance because I can't kill you, though.

steps.name: Qiubai
steps.text: It's just not worth my sword anymore.

a.text: When did she find the answer?

steps.name: Chongyue
steps.text: It seems you have made great strides in the past three years.

steps.name: Chongyue
steps.text: We...

steps.name: Huai Tianpei
steps.text: We've said too much.

steps.name: Chongyue
steps.text: I just...
Chongyue stops mid-sentence.
His opponent is injured. A few more words would give him time to adjust his breathing.
But he soon realizes that such kindness would be an insult to his opponent.
There is no such thing as a truly fair fight.
Cast away irrelevant thoughts, and give all for victory. That is what 'fair' is.

steps.name: Chongyue
steps.text: Let's begin.
Huai Tianpei clutches his fist, feeling the lines etched into his palm.
They are the marks of forty years of kung fu practice, his pride, his very emblem.
He's waited three years for this fight, but the preparation for it began on his first day studying kung fu.
A martial artist always aspires to the top.
The wind is still. The world is silent.
